## Ice for cooling versus ice for drinks

Ice used to chill bottles or display seafood is different from ice used in drinks. Drinking ice must come from a machine and bin designed for food contact and be handled with clean tools. Plan separate capacity if you use a lot of ice for cooling stock, so the drinks supply is never short. For a bar that also needs cold storage, see our [bar fridge range](/bar-fridges/).

## Noise, heat and placement

Ice machines make heat and some noise. Place the unit where there is space to ventilate, away from fryers and ovens, and where staff can reach the bin quickly. A machine tucked into a hot back room works harder and makes less ice. Our [best bar fridge guide](/guides/best-bar-fridge-australia-how-to-choose/) explains how ventilation affects any refrigeration unit.

## Matching the fridge to the venue

A pub back bar has different needs from a cafe grab-and-go cabinet. Back bar units sit low and wide so bartenders can reach bottles easily, while upright glass door fridges suit shops and cafes where customers choose their own drinks. Under bench models work where space is tight. Think about who opens the door, how often and from which side, then choose the layout that cuts walking time. Our [venue guides](/venues/cafes/) and [pub guides](/venues/pubs-hotels/) show typical setups.

## Stock rotation and loading

A fridge that is loaded well cools better. Keep gaps between rows, do not block the fan, and rotate stock so older bottles are used first. Avoid loading a large amount of warm stock at once, because the fridge needs time to pull down the temperature. Set a regular restocking time outside peak service.

## Cleaning schedule

Wipe shelves and glass daily, clean seals weekly and clear the condenser on a regular schedule. A clean fridge looks better, runs better and passes inspections more easily. Keep spare seals and shelves on hand for quick swaps; see our [shelving and baskets](/accessories-parts/shelving-baskets-trays/) range.

## Warranty and support

Trade equipment should have a clear warranty and access to parts. Ask how long the warranty lasts, what it covers and how a claim works. See our [warranty page](/warranty/) for how we handle claims.

## Stocking the fridge for service

Place the drinks you serve most at eye level, with the rest underneath. Rotate stock so older beer is used first and avoid loading a lot of warm bottles at once, because the fridge needs time to pull down the temperature. A tidy fridge keeps the door open for a shorter time, which saves cold air.

## Cleaning and care

Wipe shelves and seals regularly, empty and defrost if the model requires it, and keep the condenser clear of dust. A beer fridge that smells stale affects flavour, so clean spills straight away. Check seals for tears and replace them if the door no longer closes tightly. Spare seals and shelves are listed in our [accessories and parts](/accessories-parts/) range.

## Beer fridge for the man cave or home bar

A beer fridge is often the centrepiece of a man cave or home bar. A black or stainless finish blends in, and a glass door adds display. Think about noise, because a fridge in a living area runs all day. Our [home bar and man cave guide](/guides/home-bar-fridge-man-cave-guide/) covers layout ideas and finishes.

## Beer fridge with freezer or ice

Some beer fridges include a small freezer compartment for ice and frozen mugs. If you want a frosted glass, consider a dedicated unit from our [glass frosters](/bar-freezers/glass-frosters-specialty/). A combination unit saves space but offers limited freezer storage; see our [bar fridge freezer guide](/guides/bar-fridge-freezer-buying-guide/).

## Energy and running costs

A beer fridge runs all day, and a second fridge in a hot garage can use a noticeable amount of power. Compare energy information on the product page, keep the fridge out of the sun and keep the door closed as much as possible. If you only entertain occasionally, a smaller unit is often more economical than a large one running half-empty.

insert:
## Installation and ventilation

Commercial fridges reject more heat, so they need good ventilation. Back bar fridge and under bar models are designed with specific clearances at the front, sides or back. Check these before you place the unit in cabinetry. A unit with blocked ventilation overheats, runs constantly and fails early. Our [under bench fridge guide](/guides/under-bench-fridge-buying-guide/) explains how to plan clearance for built-in units.

## Servicing and parts

Commercial fridges are designed to be serviced. Spare parts such as seals, shelves, fans and thermostats are available, and a service schedule keeps the fridge running. Domestic fridges are often replaced rather than repaired. If uptime matters, choose a commercial unit with parts support. Our [spare parts](/accessories-parts/spare-parts/) category lists common items.

## Questions to ask a supplier

- Is the fridge rated for commercial use?
- What climate class does it have?
- How long is the warranty, and does it cover commercial use?
- Are parts available in Australia?
- What does delivery include?

Good answers to these questions give you confidence that the fridge will cope with your venue.

## What you can store in a small freezer

A small freezer suits ice, ice cream, frozen meals, garnishes and a modest amount of meat or vegetables. It does not suit bulk shopping. Pack items flat, label them and leave a little space for air. A small freezer that is neat holds more than one that is packed randomly.

## Efficiency and running costs

Smaller freezers use less power than large ones, but real use depends on the model, the room and how often the door opens. Look at the energy information on the product page and keep the freezer away from heat. Defrost manual models on schedule, because frost reduces efficiency.

## Safety and power cuts

Keep the door closed during a power cut and frozen food will stay frozen for longer. Do not refreeze food that has fully thawed. For a venue, a lock and a temperature display help protect stock. Our [door locks and gaskets](/accessories-parts/door-locks-gaskets/) range lists spares.

## Delivery and setup

Measure the doorway and the final spot. Let the unit stand upright for the time recommended in the manual before switching on, then let it reach temperature before loading. Check for transit damage on arrival. Our [delivery information](/delivery/) explains how orders reach you, and our [cheap bar fridge guide](/guides/cheap-bar-fridge-australia-what-to-check/) has budget checks that apply to freezers too.
